## About the firm
Sakshi Yadav & Co. is a Chartered Accountancy firm based in Sector 18, Noida. Founded by CA Sakshi Yadav, a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI), the firm serves salaried professionals, entrepreneurs, startups, private companies, LLPs, NGOs and NRIs.

Our practice spans direct and indirect taxation, audit and assurance, company law compliance and business advisory. Every assignment is handled with the professional standards the ICAI expects — careful documentation, independent judgment and complete confidentiality.

## CA Sakshi Yadav
Sakshi Yadav is a Chartered Accountant and a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. She founded Sakshi Yadav & Co. to offer businesses and individuals in Noida and across India the kind of attentive, partner-led advice usually reserved for large firms. Her practice covers direct and indirect taxation, audit and assurance, corporate compliance and business advisory.

## Service details
### Income Tax Return Filing & Tax Planning
URL: https://sakshiyadavandco.in/services/income-tax
File your income tax return accurately and on time with Sakshi Yadav & Co. We handle ITR-1 through ITR-7, reconcile your AIS/26AS, maximise deductions under 80C, 80D, HRA, and provide expert tax planning strategies.
Includes: ITR Filing for Salaried & Business; Old Pending ITR Filing; Capital Gains & Crypto Tax; NRI Return Filing; Income Tax Notice, Assessment & Proceeding; Tax Planning on Refund & Tax Saving; AIS/26AS Reconciliation; Advance Tax Computation.
Typical timeline: 1-3 working days.
Q: Who must file an income tax return in India?
A: You must file if your gross total income exceeds the basic exemption limit — ₹4 lakh under the new regime for FY 2025-26, or ₹2.5 lakh under the old regime (higher for senior citizens). Filing is also required if you hold foreign assets, deposited over ₹1 crore in current accounts, spent over ₹2 lakh on foreign travel, or want to carry forward losses.
Q: What is the due date for filing ITR?
A: For individuals not liable to audit, the usual due date is 31 July following the financial year (it is sometimes extended by CBDT). Taxpayers requiring a tax audit file by 31 October. A belated or revised return can be filed until 31 December.
Q: Which ITR form should I file?
A: ITR-1 suits resident individuals with salary, one house property and interest income up to ₹50 lakh. ITR-2 covers capital gains or foreign income without business income. ITR-3 is for business or professional income, including F&O trading. ITR-4 is for presumptive income under sections 44AD, 44ADA or 44AE.

### GST Registration & GST Return Filing
URL: https://sakshiyadavandco.in/services/gst-services
Sakshi Yadav & Co. provides end-to-end GST services. From obtaining your GSTIN to filing monthly, quarterly, and annual returns, we handle everything efficiently ensuring you claim maximum ITC and stay penalty-free.
Includes: New GST Registration; GSTR-1 & GSTR-3B Filing; GSTR-9 Annual Return; GST Reconciliation (GSTR-2A/2B); GST Audit; LUT Application; GST Notice Reply.
Typical timeline: 3-7 working days.
Q: How long does GST registration take?
A: A GSTIN is usually granted within 3–7 working days of filing a complete application on the GST portal, subject to Aadhaar authentication and any physical verification ordered by the department.
Q: What is the penalty for filing GSTR-3B late?
A: A late fee of ₹50 per day (₹25 CGST + ₹25 SGST) applies, capped between ₹2,000 and ₹10,000 per return depending on turnover; for nil returns it is ₹20 per day, capped at ₹500. Interest at 18% per annum is charged on unpaid tax.
Q: Can I claim input tax credit on all purchases?
A: Only on goods and services used in the course of business, supported by a valid tax invoice, reflected in your GSTR-2B, and where the supplier has paid the tax. Blocked credits under section 17(5) — such as most motor vehicles and food and beverages — are not available.

### Tax Audit & Statutory Audit
URL: https://sakshiyadavandco.in/services/tax-audit
Ensure full regulatory compliance with our audit services. Sakshi Yadav & Co. conducts Tax Audits u/s 44AB and Statutory Audits to verify your financial statements are accurate and comply with the latest tax laws.
Includes: Tax Audit u/s 44AB; Statutory Audit of Companies; NGO, Trust & Society Audit; ADT-1 — Auditor Appointment; Form 3CA/3CB & 3CD; Internal Audit; Audit Report Preparation.
Typical timeline: Case-specific.
Q: When is a tax audit under section 44AB required?
A: A tax audit is required when business turnover exceeds ₹1 crore (₹10 crore if cash receipts and payments are each within 5% of the total), when professional receipts exceed ₹50 lakh, or when presumptive-taxation cases declare lower profits than prescribed.
Q: What is the due date for the tax audit report?
A: The tax audit report in Form 3CA/3CB with Form 3CD is ordinarily due by 30 September following the end of the financial year, one month before the return due date of 31 October.
Q: Who can conduct a tax audit?
A: Only a practising Chartered Accountant holding a Certificate of Practice from the ICAI can conduct a tax audit and sign the audit report.

### TDS Return & Compliance
URL: https://sakshiyadavandco.in/services/tds-compliance
We manage your complete TDS compliance. Sakshi Yadav & Co. handles TDS computation, quarterly return filing (24Q, 26Q, 27EQ), default resolution, and issues Form 16/16A to employees and vendors.
Includes: TDS Computation & Challan; 24Q, 26Q, 27EQ Filing; Form 16/16A Generation; TAN Registration; TDS Notice Resolution.
Typical timeline: 2-5 working days.
Q: What are the due dates for TDS returns?
A: Quarterly TDS returns are due on 31 July, 31 October and 31 January for the first three quarters, and 31 May for the fourth quarter. TDS deducted must be deposited by the 7th of the following month (30 April for March).
Q: What is the TDS rate on professional fees?
A: Under section 194J, TDS is 10% on fees for professional services and 2% on fees for technical services, where payments to a person exceed ₹50,000 in a financial year (threshold applicable from 1 April 2025).
Q: What happens if a TDS return is filed late?
A: A fee of ₹200 per day applies under section 234E until the return is filed, capped at the TDS amount. A penalty of ₹10,000 to ₹1 lakh may also apply under section 271H for delays beyond one year or incorrect filings.

### Business Registration & Setup
URL: https://sakshiyadavandco.in/services/business-registration
Start your business the right way with Sakshi Yadav & Co. We help you choose the right structure and handle all registrations — from simple Proprietorships to Private Limited Companies, FSSAI food licenses, IEC for export-import, and NGO/Trust/Society formation.
Includes: Proprietorship Registration; Partnership Firm Registration; Private Limited Company (Pvt Ltd); One Person Company (OPC); FSSAI Food License; IEC — Import Export Code; NGO / Trust / Society Registration; MSME / Udyam Registration.
Typical timeline: 7-15 working days.
Q: Which business structure is right for me?
A: A proprietorship is simplest for a single owner; an LLP offers limited liability with lighter compliance; a private limited company suits businesses planning to raise capital or scale. We advise based on liability, tax, funding plans and compliance cost.
Q: What documents are needed to register a company?
A: PAN and Aadhaar of all directors and shareholders, address proof, passport-size photographs, proof of the registered office (rent agreement or ownership document with a recent utility bill) and a no-objection certificate from the property owner.
Q: Is Udyam (MSME) registration free?
A: Yes. Udyam registration on the government portal carries no fee. It needs only Aadhaar and PAN, and gives access to priority-sector lending, delayed-payment protection and government scheme benefits.

### ROC / Corporate Compliance
URL: https://sakshiyadavandco.in/services/roc-compliance
Keep your company fully compliant with MCA regulations. Sakshi Yadav & Co. handles all your ROC filings, annual returns (AOC-4, MGT-7), board meeting minutes, and statutory registers to keep you penalty-free.
Includes: Annual Return (MGT-7); Financial Statements (AOC-4); Board Meeting Minutes & Resolutions; Director Appointment / Resignation; Share Transfer & Allotment; Charge Creation / Satisfaction; Statutory Register Maintenance.
Typical timeline: 5-10 working days.
Q: What annual filings does a private limited company make with the ROC?
A: Every company files its financial statements in Form AOC-4 within 30 days of the AGM and its annual return in Form MGT-7 or MGT-7A within 60 days of the AGM, along with DIR-3 KYC for directors and ADT-1 for auditor appointment.
Q: What is the penalty for late ROC filings?
A: An additional fee of ₹100 per day of delay applies to each late form, without an upper cap, and prolonged non-filing can lead to the company being struck off and directors disqualified.
Q: What are the annual filings for an LLP?
A: An LLP files Form 11 (annual return) by 30 May and Form 8 (statement of accounts and solvency) by 30 October each year.

### Project Reports & CMA Data
URL: https://sakshiyadavandco.in/services/project-reports
Sakshi Yadav & Co. prepares professional project reports and CMA (Credit Monitoring Arrangement) data for bank loans, Mudra, SIDBI, and PMEGP. Our reports meet bank standards and are designed to maximise loan approval chances.
Includes: Project Report for Bank Loans; CMA Data Preparation; Mudra Loan Report; SIDBI / PMEGP Reports; Feasibility Studies; Business Plan Preparation.
Typical timeline: 3-5 working days.
Q: What is included in a project report for a bank loan?
A: A project report covers the business profile, cost of the project and means of finance, projected profitability, cash flows and balance sheets, break-even analysis, debt-service coverage ratio and repayment schedule — prepared to the lending bank’s format.
Q: What is CMA data?
A: Credit Monitoring Arrangement data is a set of financial statements and projections — usually covering past, current and projected years — that banks use to assess working-capital limits and term loans.
Q: Do you prepare reports for Mudra and PMEGP loans?
A: Yes. We prepare project reports for Mudra, PMEGP, CGTMSE-backed loans and SIDBI schemes, aligned with the scheme’s eligibility criteria.

### F&O / Capital Gain Tax
URL: https://sakshiyadavandco.in/services/fno-capital-gain
Sakshi Yadav & Co. handles complex ITR filings for F&O traders and investors — computing turnover, setting off losses, claiming expenses, and ensuring full tax compliance for stock market participants.
Includes: F&O Turnover Computation; ITR-3 Filing for F&O Traders; Long-Term & Short-Term Capital Gains; Crypto / Virtual Digital Asset Tax; Loss Set-Off & Carry Forward; P&L from Broker Reports.
Typical timeline: 2-4 working days.
Q: Is F&O trading income treated as business income?
A: Yes. Profit or loss from futures and options is non-speculative business income, reported in ITR-3. Turnover is computed as the aggregate of absolute profits and losses, which decides whether a tax audit is required.
Q: How are capital gains on listed shares taxed?
A: For transfers on or after 23 July 2024, short-term gains on listed equity are taxed at 20% and long-term gains (held over 12 months) at 12.5% on gains exceeding ₹1.25 lakh in a year.
Q: Can I carry forward F&O losses?
A: Yes. Non-speculative business losses can be carried forward for eight years and set off against business income, provided the return is filed by the due date.

Inter-state suppliers of goods, e-commerce sellers and certain other categories must register regardless of turnover. We can assess your position before you apply.

A: With documents in order, a private limited company is usually incorporated within 7–15 working days through the MCA SPICe+ form, which covers name reservation, DIN, PAN, TAN and the Certificate of Incorporation. Digital Signature Certificates for directors are obtained first.

## Articles
### How to File ITR Online: A Complete Guide for Salaried Employees (FY 2025-26)
URL: https://sakshiyadavandco.in/blog/how-to-file-itr-online-salaried-employees | Income Tax | Published 2025-09-15

Filing your Income Tax Return (ITR) online doesn't have to be stressful. With a bit of preparation and the right guidance, most salaried employees can get it done in under an hour. Here's a simple, plain-English walkthrough of the entire process.

Who must file ITR?
If your gross income exceeds ₹4 lakh under the new tax regime for FY 2025-26 (or ₹2.5 lakh under the old regime), you are legally required to file an ITR — even if no tax is owed. Additionally, if you have foreign assets, multiple sources of income, or want to carry forward a capital loss, filing is mandatory regardless of income.

Which ITR form should you use?
For most salaried employees with one employer, one house property, and no business income, ITR-1 (Sahaj) is the right form. If you have capital gains from stocks or mutual funds, you'll need ITR-2. Freelancers and consultants earning professional income should file ITR-3 or ITR-4 (Sugam).

Documents you'll need
Before you start, keep these ready: your Form 16 from your employer, AIS (Annual Information Statement) from the income tax portal, bank statements, investment proofs under Section 80C (LIC, PPF, ELSS), 80D (health insurance premiums), home loan interest certificate, and your PAN and Aadhaar.

Step-by-step filing process
Visit incometax.gov.in and log in with your PAN. Go to e-File → Income Tax Returns → File Income Tax Return. Select Assessment Year 2026-27 (for income earned in FY 2025-26) and choose Online mode. Select the appropriate ITR form. The portal pre-fills most of your data — verify it against your Form 16 and AIS carefully. Enter your deductions, compute tax, verify using Aadhaar OTP or Net Banking, and submit. You'll receive an acknowledgment (ITR-V) in your email within minutes.

Deadlines and penalties
The usual last date is July 31 for individuals. Filing after this attracts a late fee of ₹1,000 (if income ≤ ₹5 lakh) or ₹5,000. More importantly, late filing means you cannot carry forward losses from stocks or business, and you may face interest under Section 234A.

Pro tip: Always download and cross-check your AIS before filing. Many clients get notices simply because they forgot to report a fixed deposit interest or mutual fund redemption that already appears in the AIS.

If you have capital gains, NRI income, foreign assets, or received a tax notice — it's best to get professional help. The cost of getting it wrong is always higher than the professional fees.

---

### GST Registration in India: Who Needs It, Threshold Limits & How to Apply
URL: https://sakshiyadavandco.in/blog/gst-registration-threshold-limits-how-to-apply | GST | Published 2025-09-08

GST registration is not just a legal requirement — it's actually a business advantage if you're dealing with other registered businesses. Let's break down who needs it, what the thresholds are, and what the process looks like.

Threshold limits for GST registration
For businesses selling goods: ₹40 lakh annual turnover (₹20 lakh in some states like Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Nagaland). For service providers: ₹20 lakh turnover. Special category states have lower thresholds of ₹10 lakh for services. These are aggregate turnover limits — that means all your India-wide sales combined.

Cases where registration is mandatory regardless of turnover
Even if you earn below the threshold, you must register if you: sell goods inter-state (across state borders), sell through e-commerce platforms like Amazon or Flipkart, are an e-commerce operator, need to pay GST under reverse charge mechanism, or are a non-resident taxable person operating in India.

Documents required for GST registration
For proprietorships: PAN card, Aadhaar card, bank account statement, photograph, and proof of principal place of business (electricity bill or rent agreement). For companies: certificate of incorporation, MoA/AoA, board resolution, director's PAN & Aadhaar, and bank statement.

The registration process
Visit gst.gov.in and fill Form GST REG-01 with your business details, bank account info, and upload documents. You'll receive an Application Reference Number (ARN) by SMS and email. After verification (usually 3-7 working days), your GSTIN is issued. If the GST officer raises queries, respond via the portal within 7 working days or the application gets rejected.

Benefits of being GST registered
You can charge GST on your invoices and claim Input Tax Credit (ITC) on your business purchases — which directly reduces your cost. It also makes you a credible business partner for other registered companies that need tax invoices from their suppliers.

Important: Doing business without GST registration when you're liable is an offence. The penalty is ₹10,000 or the amount of tax evaded — whichever is higher. If the GST department detects it, you'll also owe all the back taxes with interest.

### Old Tax Regime vs New Tax Regime (FY 2025-26): Which One Saves You More?
URL: https://sakshiyadavandco.in/blog/old-vs-new-tax-regime-which-saves-more | Income Tax | Published 2025-08-28

Every year, one of the most common questions we get is: "Which tax regime should I choose?" The answer depends on your income level, how many deductions you can claim, and your lifestyle. Let's lay out the facts.

Tax slabs comparison for FY 2025-26

Old Regime: Up to ₹2.5L — Nil | ₹2.5L-₹5L — 5% | ₹5L-₹10L — 20% | Above ₹10L — 30%

New Regime (Default): Up to ₹4L — Nil | ₹4L-₹8L — 5% | ₹8L-₹12L — 10% | ₹12L-₹16L — 15% | ₹16L-₹20L — 20% | ₹20L-₹24L — 25% | Above ₹24L — 30%

Under the new regime, the Section 87A rebate makes tax nil for resident individuals with taxable income up to ₹12 lakh — effectively ₹12.75 lakh for salaried employees after the ₹75,000 standard deduction.

Note: The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaces the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026. Section references here are to the 1961 Act, which governs returns for FY 2025-26.

Who benefits from the old regime?
The old regime is better if you have significant deductions: HRA (House Rent Allowance) for rent-paying employees, ₹1.5 lakh under Section 80C (LIC, PPF, ELSS, home loan principal), home loan interest (up to ₹2 lakh under Section 24b), health insurance under Section 80D, and NPS contribution under Section 80CCD.

A quick example: Salaried employee earning ₹12 lakh, claiming ₹1.5L (80C) + ₹1.8L (HRA) + ₹2L (home loan interest) + ₹25K (80D) = total deductions of ₹5.55L. Taxable income in old regime = ₹6.45L, tax ≈ ₹43,000. In new regime, taxable income = ₹12L, tax ≈ ₹90,000. The old regime saves ₹47,000 here.

Who benefits from the new regime?
If you have minimal deductions, are renting informally (no formal HRA), have no home loan, or your investments are small — the new regime's simpler slabs often work out better. For someone earning ₹7 lakh with no major deductions, the tax is literally ₹0 under the new regime thanks to the 87A rebate.

The default trap: From FY 2023-24, the new regime became the default. If you don't explicitly choose the old regime, you'll automatically be put in the new one. To choose the old regime, you must file Form 10-IE (for business income) or select it when filing your ITR.

Our advice: Do a rough calculation both ways before filing. For most salaried people with home loans and HRA, the old regime often wins if income is between ₹10-20 lakh. For simpler earners without big deductions, the new regime is usually better. When in doubt, consult a qualified professional — the right choice can save you tens of thousands of rupees.

---

### TDS on Salary, Rent & Professional Fees: Rates, Thresholds & Filing Guide
URL: https://sakshiyadavandco.in/blog/tds-rates-thresholds-salary-rent-professional-fees | TDS | Published 2025-08-15

Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) is a mechanism where the payer deducts tax before making a payment and deposits it with the government. It's not optional — failing to deduct or deposit TDS on time leads to penalties, disallowed business expenses, and interest charges.

Common TDS sections and rates:

Section 192 — Salary: Rate based on the employee's applicable income tax slab (no fixed rate). Threshold: No minimum; deduct if annual salary exceeds basic exemption limit.

Section 194C — Contractor/Sub-contractor payments: 1% (individual/HUF) or 2% (others). Single payment threshold: ₹30,000; annual aggregate: ₹1 lakh.

Section 194J — Professional fees: 10%; technical fees: 2%. Threshold: ₹50,000 in a financial year (from 1 April 2025).

Section 194I — Rent: 10% for land/building; 2% for machinery. Threshold: ₹50,000 per month.

Section 194Q — Purchase of goods: 0.1% if buyer's annual turnover > ₹10 crore. Threshold: Purchase > ₹50 lakh from one seller.

When to deduct and deposit TDS
Deduct TDS at the time of payment or at the time of credit — whichever is earlier. Deposit to the government by the 7th of the following month (except March, where the deadline is April 30). For government deductors, it's the same day of deduction.

Quarterly TDS returns
You must file quarterly TDS returns: 24Q for salary, 26Q for non-salary payments to residents, 27Q for payments to non-residents, 27EQ for TCS. Due dates: Q1 (Apr-Jun) → July 31 | Q2 (Jul-Sep) → October 31 | Q3 (Oct-Dec) → January 31 | Q4 (Jan-Mar) → May 31.

Form 16 and 16A
After filing quarterly returns, you must issue Form 16 (for employees) and Form 16A (for others) showing the TDS deducted and deposited on their behalf. Employees use this to file their ITR. Failure to issue Form 16 on time attracts ₹100 per day penalty.

What happens if you don't deduct TDS?
The entire expense becomes disallowed — meaning you can't claim it as a business deduction. You also owe interest at 1% per month (failure to deduct) or 1.5% per month (failure to deposit), plus a penalty of ₹10,000 to ₹1 lakh under Section 271H. The income tax department does scrutiny assessments specifically for TDS defaults, especially on rent and contractor payments.

TDS compliance might seem tedious, but it's one of the areas where businesses get caught most often. Keeping a simple TDS calendar and working with a qualified professional for quarterly filing is the smartest investment for any business paying more than a few lakh rupees a year.

---

### Received an Income Tax Notice? Here's Exactly What to Do
URL: https://sakshiyadavandco.in/blog/income-tax-notice-what-to-do | Income Tax | Published 2025-08-05

Every year, millions of taxpayers receive income tax notices. Most people panic — but the reality is that a significant portion of these notices are automated, routine, and can be resolved easily if you respond correctly and on time.

The most common types of income tax notices:

Intimation u/s 143(1): This is the most common. It's an automated communication after your ITR is processed. It may show a demand (tax payable) or a refund. Common reasons: mismatch between your ITR and Form 26AS, incorrect computation, or deductions not matching. This is NOT a scrutiny notice. You can respond online.

Notice u/s 139(9): Sent when your ITR has a defect — like selecting the wrong form, a field that doesn't add up, or missing a mandatory schedule. You have 15 days to correct and re-file.

Notice u/s 148/148A: Sent when the IT department believes income has escaped assessment (i.e., you earned income and didn't declare it). This is a serious notice. Always get professional help here.

Notice u/s 143(2): Scrutiny notice. The department wants to verify specific claims in your return. This triggers a full assessment proceeding and requires detailed documentation.

What to do immediately after receiving a notice:
Don't ignore it — there are strict response deadlines. Log in to incometax.gov.in and find the notice under "Pending Actions" or "e-Proceedings". Read it carefully to understand the specific reason. Gather your relevant documents — bank statements, investment proofs, AIS, Form 16. If it's a simple mismatch, you can respond directly online. For anything beyond a 143(1) intimation, consult a qualified professional.

Documents to always keep ready:
Save your ITR acknowledgment (ITR-V) for at least 6 years. Keep Form 26AS / AIS printouts for the year. Retain investment receipts, rent agreements, loan certificates, and salary slips. Anything you claimed as a deduction or exemption should have supporting documentation.

Never miss the deadline. Most notices give you 15-30 days to respond. Missing the deadline converts a simple issue into a contested assessment. If you're unsure about a notice, the safest approach is to call your professional the same day you receive it — most issues are sorted within a week when handled promptly.

---

### GSTR-1, GSTR-3B & GSTR-9: Which GST Return Do You Need to File?
URL: https://sakshiyadavandco.in/blog/gstr-1-vs-gstr-3b-vs-gstr-9 | GST | Published 2025-07-25

If you're newly registered under GST, the compliance calendar can feel overwhelming. GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, GSTR-9... what is each one, and when is it due? Let's cut through the confusion.

GSTR-1 — Outward Supply Statement
This is where you declare all your sales (outward supplies) for the month or quarter. Include B2B invoices, B2C sales, credit notes, debit notes, and export invoices. Your customers see your GSTR-1 in their GSTR-2A/2B to claim Input Tax Credit (ITC). Getting GSTR-1 right is critical — mistakes here mean your customer can't claim ITC, which damages your business relationships.

Due date: 11th of the following month (monthly filers) or 13th after the end of the quarter (QRMP scheme filers with turnover < ₹5 crore).

GSTR-3B — Monthly Summary Return
This is a self-declared summary return where you report total outward supplies, total ITC claimed, and pay the GST payable. You must pay the tax liability by the due date even if your full GSTR-1 isn't ready. Think of it as the payment return.

Due date: 20th of the following month (large taxpayers) or 22nd/24th of the following month (smaller states vs. other states, for quarterly filers).

GSTR-9 — Annual Return
Filed once a year, GSTR-9 consolidates all your monthly returns for the financial year. It reconciles your outward supplies and ITC — any differences from your monthly returns need to be explained. Mandatory for taxpayers with annual turnover > ₹2 crore. Optional for those below ₹2 crore.

Due date: December 31 of the following financial year.

GSTR-2A and GSTR-2B — ITC Tracking
These are not returns you file — they're auto-generated statements showing you the ITC available based on your suppliers' GSTR-1 filings. GSTR-2A is dynamic (updates as suppliers file). GSTR-2B is static (generated on the 14th of each month and doesn't change). Most professional firms now use GSTR-2B for reconciliation as it's more reliable.

Common GST compliance mistakes:
Not filing GSTR-1 on time (your buyers can't claim ITC), claiming more ITC than what appears in GSTR-2B, not reversing ITC on exempt supplies or personal-use goods, forgetting reverse charge liability (RCM), and missing the annual return deadline.

Late fees: ₹50/day (₹25 CGST + ₹25 SGST) for delays in GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B, subject to a maximum of ₹5,000 for regular taxpayers. For nil returns, the late fee is ₹20/day. Interest on tax liability: 18% per annum from the due date of GSTR-3B.

GST compliance is genuinely manageable when you have a system. Most businesses benefit from outsourcing their monthly GST filing to a professional — it's typically priced between ₹500-₹2,000/month depending on transaction volume, which is far less than a late fee or a notice.

---

### Sole Proprietorship vs Private Limited Company vs LLP: Which Business Structure Should You Choose?
URL: https://sakshiyadavandco.in/blog/proprietorship-vs-private-limited-vs-llp | Business Registration | Published 2025-07-10

One of the first decisions every new business owner faces is: what structure should I register under? Each option has different tax implications, compliance requirements, liability protection, and future fundraising potential. Here's a practical breakdown.

Sole Proprietorship
The simplest structure — your business and you are legally the same entity. No formal registration required (though you may need GST, FSSAI, or Shop & Establishment registration depending on your business). Perfect for freelancers, small traders, local shops, and service providers just starting out.

Advantages: Zero setup cost, minimal compliance, all profit is yours. Disadvantages: Unlimited personal liability (your personal assets can be attached if there's a business debt), limited access to bank credit, no legal separation between you and the business.

Private Limited Company (Pvt Ltd)
The most credible and investor-friendly structure. A separate legal entity from its shareholders — your personal assets are protected (limited liability). Minimum 2 directors and 2 shareholders (can be the same people).

Advantages: Limited liability, easy to raise funding, high credibility with clients and vendors, can issue ESOPs, best for B2B businesses. Disadvantages: Higher compliance cost (ROC filings, statutory audit mandatory, MCA forms), minimum ₹15,000-₹20,000/year in compliance costs, more paperwork to close or exit.

Limited Liability Partnership (LLP)
The best of both worlds for professional service firms (professional firms, consultants, architects). Partners have limited liability, but compliance is lighter than a Pvt Ltd. Minimum 2 partners.

Advantages: Limited liability, flexible profit sharing, no mandatory statutory audit (below ₹40L turnover), lighter compliance than Pvt Ltd. Disadvantages: Cannot issue equity shares (can't raise venture capital), less preferred by investors.

Which one should you choose?

Choose Sole Proprietorship if: You're just starting, turnover is under ₹40 lakh, you have no partners, and you want zero compliance burden.

Choose LLP if: You're in a professional service business (consulting, accounting, architecture), have 2+ partners, and want liability protection without heavy compliance.

Choose Private Limited if: You're a startup seeking investment, you need high credibility with large clients (especially corporates or government), you plan to hire employees on a large scale, or you want to list on a stock exchange someday.

Tax comparison:
Sole Proprietorship: Taxed at individual slab rates (up to 30%). LLP: Taxed at 30% flat (plus AMT provisions). Private Limited: Taxed at 25% (if turnover < ₹400 crore) or 22% (new concessional regime under 115BAA, but surrenders exemptions).

Our practical observation: Most small businesses start as proprietorships and convert to Pvt Ltd when they either cross ₹1 crore turnover or start dealing with corporate clients. The conversion itself is a simple process. Don't over-engineer your structure at the start — get the basics right first.

---

### GST for Freelancers & Consultants in India: Everything You Need to Know
URL: https://sakshiyadavandco.in/blog/gst-for-freelancers-and-consultants | GST | Published 2025-06-20

Freelancers and independent consultants are one of the fastest-growing segments in India's workforce — but GST compliance for them is often misunderstood. Let's set the record straight.

Does a freelancer need GST registration?
If your annual income from services exceeds ₹20 lakh (₹10 lakh in some states), you must register for GST. However, there are cases where registration is mandatory regardless of turnover: if you're providing services to clients outside India (export of services), if your services fall under a specific category that requires compulsory registration, or if you want to claim ITC on business expenses (laptop, software, etc.).

What rate of GST applies?
Most professional services (IT services, content writing, marketing, design, etc.) attract 18% GST. If you're registered, you must add 18% GST to every invoice for Indian clients and deposit it with the government after claiming ITC on your expenses.

Export of services — zero-rated supply
Good news for freelancers working with overseas clients: services exported to foreign clients (where payment is received in foreign currency) are treated as zero-rated exports. This means no GST is charged on such invoices. You need to file a LUT (Letter of Undertaking) with the GST department before invoicing foreign clients, and you can claim refund of ITC on your business inputs.

How to raise a compliant GST invoice?
Every GST invoice must include: your firm's name, GSTIN, address, invoice number and date, client name and GSTIN (for B2B), description of service, HSN/SAC code, taxable value, GST rate (CGST + SGST or IGST), and total amount. Missing any of these elements makes it a non-compliant invoice.

Input Tax Credit — what you can claim
If you're GST-registered, you can claim ITC on business expenses: your laptop, software subscriptions, internet connection, co-working space rent, stationery, etc. This effectively reduces your GST liability — you pay only the net GST (output tax minus input tax credit).

Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM)
Some services trigger RCM — where the recipient (not the supplier) pays GST. As a freelancer, you may be liable to pay GST under RCM on services received from unregistered vendors above ₹5,000/day (legal services, certain transportation, etc.). This is a common area of non-compliance for consultants.

Our recommendation: If you're a freelancer earning between ₹15-30 lakh per year and working with a mix of Indian and foreign clients, a GST-registered setup with quarterly filings managed by a qualified professional is the most tax-efficient approach. The ITC alone often offsets 80-90% of your GST burden.
